one_line: Kaivarta leader Divya and Pala king Ramapala clash and contend over Varendra in early 12th‑century north Bengal.

appearance.age_look: Divya looks around 30, lean and wiry; Ramapala looks around 40, tall and solidly built.
appearance.face: Divya has an oval face, wheat‑brown complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, intense narrow eyes with a serious, slightly guarded expression; Ramapala has a broader face, slightly lighter brown complexion, strong jaw, full but tidy beard and moustache, calm large eyes and a composed, dignified default expression.
appearance.hair: Divya’s black hair is medium length, tied back in a small topknot at the back of the crown with loose strands near the temples; Ramapala’s black hair is longer, gathered smoothly into a high, neat topknot, partly hidden by his headcloth and crown band.
appearance.costume: Divya wears a practical mid‑11th/12th‑century north‑eastern Indian warrior outfit: a knee‑length off‑white cotton uttariya wrapped tightly around the torso like a fitted tunic, over a deep‑green, slightly quilted, sleeveless cloth vamsha‑style coat; he has a wrapped lower garment like a dhoti in muted brick‑red with a narrow cream border, pleated in front and hitched to mid‑calf for movement, plus a plain dark‑brown cloth belt; his feet have simple brown leather sandals; ornaments are minimal—thin copper armlets on both arms and a single small copper earring in the left ear. Ramapala wears a more elaborate royal Pala ensemble: a long, soft golden‑yellow silk uttariya draped across the chest and over the left shoulder, under which a fitted, long‑sleeved dark‑indigo upper garment (stitched, courtly style) reaches to mid‑thigh; his lower garment is a rich maroon silk dhoti with broad woven gold borders, wrapped elegantly to ankle length; he has a narrow, patterned waist sash in deep blue and gold, and finely strapped dark‑brown sandals; his jewellery is dignified but not excessive—a slim gold torque, a pair of small gold earrings, and two gold bangles on each wrist; on his head he wears a soft maroon pagri‑style cloth wrap with a simple gold band (a modest crown band) at the front.
appearance.signature: Divya carries a long bamboo spear with an iron leaf‑shaped head and simple iron butt cap, its shaft wrapped with a short strip of dark cloth near the grip, while Ramapala bears a slightly curved steel sword in a plain dark‑brown scabbard with subtle gold fittings, worn at his left hip on a dark leather belt.

ref_desc: Divya is a lean, wheat‑brown north‑Bengal warrior with a short beard, medium black hair in a small topknot, off‑white torso wrap, deep‑green sleeveless coat, brick‑red dhoti and bamboo spear, while Ramapala is a taller, dignified king with fuller beard, high topknot under a maroon headwrap with gold band, golden‑yellow silk drape over indigo tunic, maroon gold‑bordered dhoti and curved sword at his hip, both in off‑white, deep green, brick red, indigo and golden yellow tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of two early‑12th‑century north‑Bengal men standing side by side: Divya and Ramapala, each clearly distinct but harmonised. Divya is around 30, lean and wiry, with a wheat‑brown complexion, oval face, sharp nose, intense narrow eyes and a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache; his black hair is medium length, tied back in a small topknot at the back of the crown with a few loose strands at the temples. Dress him in an off‑white cotton wrap tightly bound around his torso like a fitted tunic, over a deep‑green sleeveless slightly quilted cloth warrior coat; give him a brick‑red dhoti with a narrow cream border, wrapped and pleated in front and hitched to mid‑calf, held by a plain dark‑brown cloth belt; add simple brown leather sandals, thin copper armlets and a single small copper earring in his left ear. Place a long bamboo spear with an iron leaf‑shaped head in his right hand, with a short dark cloth wrap near the grip and an iron butt cap. Beside him, Ramapala stands taller and more solidly built, around 40, with a slightly lighter brown complexion, broad face, strong jaw, full but tidy beard and moustache, and calm large eyes giving a composed, dignified look; his black hair is drawn into a high neat topknot partly covered by a soft maroon pagri‑style headwrap with a simple gold band across the front like a modest crown. Dress him in a golden‑yellow silk uttariya draped across his chest and over the left shoulder, worn over a fitted long‑sleeved dark‑indigo upper garment reaching mid‑thigh; his lower garment is a rich maroon silk dhoti with broad woven gold borders, wrapped to ankle length, with a narrow deep‑blue and gold patterned waist sash; give him slender gold jewellery—a torque, small earrings and two bangles on each wrist—and dark‑brown strapped sandals. At his left hip, show a slightly curved steel sword in a plain dark‑brown scabbard with subtle gold fittings, suspended from a dark leather belt. Use a cohesive palette of off‑white, deep green, brick red, indigo and golden yellow, and pose them facing forward with clear views of their faces, hair, full costumes and weapons for consistent redrawing in multiple panels.
